intended_object: Given a ring congruence c on the opposite ring Rᵐᵒᵖ, the corresponding ring congruence on R, with a ~ b iff c(op b, op a). This is the inverse map of the order isomorphism between congruences on R and on Rᵐᵒᵖ (from the docstring and the module doc).
explanation: The definition reuses `Con.unop` for the underlying multiplicative congruence. That relation is (a, b) ↦ c (op b) (op a), as the docstring says, and `unop_iff` holds by `Iff.rfl`. Compatibility with addition comes straight from `c.add`, since addition on Rᵐᵒᵖ is the addition of R carried over unchanged. Because congruences are symmetric, the swap of arguments makes no mathematical difference; it is the same congruence as {(a, b) : (op a, op b) ∈ c}. The construction only assumes `[Add R] [Mul R]`, which is the most general setting for `RingCon`. Together with `RingCon.op`, it gives the order isomorphism `opOrderIso`. This is the standard transport of a congruence across the opposite ring, stated in full generality. It is close to a technical companion of `op`, but it is still a well-defined mathematical construction, the inverse half of the correspondence, so the verdict is faithful.
